record.original_question: For f ∈ S^dV, let X be the scheme associated to a generalized additive decomposition (GAD) of minimal length. Is reg(X) ≤ d? More generally, which conditions on f guarantee existence of a GAD whose associated scheme has low regularity?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. For f ∈ S d V , let X be the scheme associated to a GAD of minimal length. Is reg(X) ≤ d? In general, determine what conditions on f guarantee the existence of a GAD whose associated scheme has low regularity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space, and let $S^{\bullet}V = \bigoplus_{d \ge 0} S^d V$ denote the symmetric algebra on $V$, whose elements of degree $d$ are identified with degree-$d$ homogeneous polynomials (forms). For a form $f \in S^d V$, a generalized additive decomposition (GAD) of $f$ is an expression
$$ f \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{r} \ell_i^{\,d - m_i}\, g_i, $$
where $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_r \in V$ are pairwise non-proportional linear forms, $1 \le m_i \le d$, and each $g_i \in S^{m_i}V$ is a form of degree $m_i$. To such a GAD one associates a $0$-dimensional subscheme $X \subset \mathbb{P}(V^*)$, supported at the points $[\ell_i]$, whose local component at $[\ell_i]$ is the scheme defined by the apolar ideal of $g_i$ (viewed after a change of coordinates centered at $[\ell_i]$). The length of the GAD is $\mathrm{length}(X) = \sum_i \dim_K (S^{\bullet}V / \mathrm{Ann}(g_i))$, and a GAD is said to be of minimal length if no GAD of $f$ has smaller length. The Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $X$ is denoted $\mathrm{reg}(X)$.

(a) For every $f \in S^d V$ and every $0$-dimensional scheme $X$ arising from a GAD of $f$ of minimal length, does the inequality $\mathrm{reg}(X) \le d$ hold?

(b) More generally, determine sufficient conditions on $f \in S^d V$ that guarantee the existence of a GAD of $f$ whose associated scheme $X$ has low Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity (e.g. $\mathrm{reg}(X) \le d$).
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work on schemes evinced by generalized additive decompositions establishes the bound reg(X) ≤ d in special cases: minimal-length tangential decompositions always evince d-regular schemes, and irredundant apolar schemes of length at most 2d+1 are d-regular. However, irredundant schemes apolar to a form need not be d-regular in general, so the question for arbitrary minimal-length GADs is not fully settled, and the general characterization in part (b) remains open.

status_evidence.title: On schemes evinced by generalized additive decompositions and their regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Tangential decompositions of minimal length are always d-regular, as well as irredundant apolar schemes of length at most 2d+1. Irredundant schemes need not be d-regular unless evinced by special GADs.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results: minimal tangential GADs and short irredundant apolar schemes are d-regular, but not all minimal GADs are known to yield d-regular schemes.

status_evidence.title: Determinantal computation of minimal local GADs
status_evidence.snippet: A linear algebra method for measuring the GAD size; minimal GAD-rank equals rank of suitable Catalecticant matrices under regularity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research on minimal GADs and associated regularity conditions, indicating the general problem is still being investigated.
